title: Illinois BIPA — Informed consent before collecting biometric identifiers
description: The informed-consent and private-right-of-action provisions of the Illinois Biometric Information Privacy Act. Paraphrase pending verification against the primary statute text — hence 'Community' confidence.

history.note: Initial Phase 2A seed content. Specific statutory damages figures ($1,000/$5,000 per violation) are commonly cited but not independently verified against the primary statute text in this pass.

control_reference: 740 ILCS 14/15 (notice and consent); 740 ILCS 14/20 (private right of action)
control_text: Private entities must provide written notice and obtain written consent before collecting, capturing, or otherwise obtaining a person's biometric identifiers or biometric information (fingerprints, retina/iris scans, voiceprints, face/hand geometry scans). The statute creates a private right of action allowing individuals to sue for statutory damages without needing to show actual injury.

relationships.reason: This control's own text is the definition of what the evidence record must capture.
